question: By maternal descent, Mughals were descendants of?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Genghis Khan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

__
 
• Mughals:

 
 
• The Mughals were descendants of two great lineages of rulers.
 
• From their mother’s side, they were descendants of Genghis Khan (died 1227), the Mongol ruler who ruled over parts of China and Central Asia.
 
• From their father’s side, they were the successors of Timur (who died in 1404), the ruler of Iran, Iraq and modern-day Turkey.
 
• However, the Mughals did not like to be called Mughal or Mongol.
 
• This was because Genghis Khan’s memory was associated with the massacre of innumerable people.
 
• It was also linked with the Uzbeks, their Mongol competitors.
 
• On the other hand, the Mughals were proud of their Timurid ancestry, not least of all because their great ancestor had captured Delhi in 1398.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Timur**

 
 
• In 1398 A.D., the Timur or Tamerlane invaded India during the reign of Nasiruddin Mahmud, the last king of the Tughlaq dynasty.
 
• Attacking the Delhi Sultanate ruled by Sultan Nasir-ud-Din Mahmud Shah Tughluq.
 
• He started his journey from Samarkand. After crossing the Sindh river, he entered Punjab.
 
• He crossed Indus and captured Multan, and just walked over to Delhi without much resistance.
 
• Tamerlane was a Turco-Mongol, who founded the Timurid Empire.
 
 

 
• Alexander__

 __
 
• Alexander__, the invaded India in the year __326 BC__.
 
• In 326 BC, Alexander invaded India, after crossing the river Indus he advanced towards Taxila.
 
• The Battle of the Hydaspes was fought in 326 BC between Alexander the Great and King Porus of the Paurava kingdom on the banks of the Jhelum River (known to the Greeks as Hydaspes) in the Punjab region.
 
• Alexander captured Porus and, like the other local rulers he had defeated, allowed him to continue to govern his territory.
 
• Alexander the Great was a king (basileus) of the ancient Greek kingdom of Macedon.
